title: Extract async fanout strategy and adaptive warmup for worker pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Refactor the async ingestion pipeline to pull out a pluggable fanout strategy and introduce an adaptive warmup mechanism for worker pools. Unify retry contract semantics across Redis and Kafka connectors to avoid duplicate deliveries during transient failures, and introduce a credit-based backpressure controller to reduce head-of-line blocking. This ticket is focused on code structure and low-risk logic changes (no user-facing API changes).
acceptance_criteria: FanoutStrategy interface extracted with Redis and Kafka implementations behind a feature flag
AdaptiveWarmup policy implemented: new workers receive staged inflight credits to avoid cold-start bursts
Retry contract unified: idempotency token propagation and at-least-once-to-ordered-delivery mapping documented and implemented
End-to-end benchmarks show <=5% tail-latency regression and >=15% reduction in retry amplification under failure scenarios
Automated unit and integration tests cover connector failure, leader rebalancing, and warmup transitions
comments: 2026-01-15 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff. Initial spike completed. Confirmed primary pain: worker cold-start bursts causing downstream KV cache thrash and retry storms. Draft design in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Async+Fanout+and+Warmup
2026-01-22 - Marco Li: Implemented prototype FanoutStrategy interface and a simple round-robin Redis/Kafka adapter in feature branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/12345

2026-01-27 - Engineering review: decided to keep connector-specific batching inside connector adapter and expose only ingress hooks for credit allocation. Trade-off: slightly more adapter surface area vs clearer runtime boundaries.

2026-01-30 - Load testing (staging): observed retry amplification when worker restart coincided with upstream replay. Introduced idempotency token header propagation and lightweight dedupe in consumer shim as mitigation.

2026-02-03 - QA: wrote integration test that simulates broker flapping and verifies no more than one duplicate delivery per message within 30s window. Test linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/actions/workflows/integration-warmup.yaml

2026-02-06 - Perf: benchmark results attached to PR show 18% lower peak retry traffic and 12% lower median queue drain time. We still have a 4% tail-latency regression at 99th percentile — investigating kernel selection in runtime-1.24
2026-02-08 - Security review (informal): no secrets changes. Confirmed that KMS/HSM integrations unaffected. Added note to security_review_required=false

2026-02-09 - Marco Li: Preparing rollout plan. Will gate FanoutStrategy behind feature flag 'fanout-v2' and enable for 10% of traffic for 24h, monitor 'ingress.duplicate_rate' and 'worker.inflight_jitter' metrics before progressive ramp
